content: The hum of a thousand servers was the only prayer this cathedral of ones and zeroes ever heard—low, constant, like the breath of some vast buried beast. Flickering blue LEDs cast long, prison-bar shadows across cold tile floors, where a lone janitor pushed a mop bucket past towering black monoliths pulsing with the secrets of the damned. Somewhere in the labyrinth, a faulty rack coughed static into the silence, and the air tasted of ozone and bad decisions. I found her in Cage 13, backlit by the sick glow of a compromised terminal, her fingers dancing over a keyboard like she was picking a corpse’s pocket. She didn’t look up. “They erased his footprint,” she said, voice flat as a dead line. “But data leaves scars.” A single red light blinked where it shouldn’t—someone’s ghost in the machine, and me, just another shadow chasing it down the cold, endless aisles.
